name: Jody Clay
life: “I still remember telling my spouse the time I actually had for Sunday.” On Thursday, near Juniper Street, Jody knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I love his company but I also need Sundays for my own marriage. I'm joining once a month on a fixed date.
appearance: Jody has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for thick, tightly coiled hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an unlined tan jacket with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Jody folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Jody can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Jody can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To offer a sustainable monthly Sunday.
family: Jo March is Jody’s parent’s cousin. Jody can always ask for five minutes alone. Jo asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The widow's razor*, Jo says, “I was forbidden to cut girls' hair here. That woman lent me the razor for my first paying customer.”
connections: Quinn Park. A sustainable family date gives the social worker a better measure of companionship than a timed task.
